paper_title: Extending the Centerpoint Theorem to Multiple Points
classifications: Theory of computation → Design and analysis of algorithms
statement: From an algorithmic point of view, the bottleneck for the running time of our approach is Lemma 8. The current methods result in O(n log3 n) time. While solutions to such kinds of problems can usually only be verified in Θ(n log n) time (see, e.g., [2, 16]), a linear-time algorithm, like for centerpoints [8], is conceivable. For arbitrarily many points, it seems tedious but doable to apply similar approaches as in the proof of Theorem 9. Is there a good bound on the running time independent of the size of |Q|?
